At the ground-space identification in step 2.1, zero energy for a sum of positive weighted commuting penalty projections forces every penalty to vanish, so every stabilizer has eigenvalue +1.

Conversely, a vector in every stabilizer +1 eigenspace has every penalty zero and hence H_K=0, as used in step 2.1. This is the ground-space identification, not a converse perturbation or stability theorem.

The stabilizer projection in 1.1 may have rank greater than one. The parity calculations in 2.1–2.2 and penalty calculations in 3.1–4.1 apply to every ground vector; no unique-ground-state hypothesis is used.
As E decreases to zero, sinh(a sqrt(E)) is O(sqrt(E)); the density therefore has no lower-endpoint divergence, as used in steps 2.1 and 4.1.
The lower endpoint is locally integrable by the square-root behavior in step 4.1; at infinity the Gaussian bounds in steps 2.1 and 4.1 are integrable.
